analysis: Ophthalmological ointments are designed for application to the eye and must meet specific requirements to ensure safety and efficacy. They may contain solid particles, but these must be of a controlled size to avoid irritation or damage to the eye. Sterility is crucial for ophthalmic preparations to prevent infections. Pyrogen testing is typically not required for ophthalmic ointments, as pyrogens are more of a concern for injectable products. Ophthalmic ointments can be water-in-oil (W/O) emulsions, and while many excipients are fatty to provide the necessary consistency and stability, it is not an absolute requirement that all excipients be fatty.
